classes.name: Ständeratswahlen
classes.note: Each canton is counted once per National Council term, using the Federal Assembly's list of National Council election years. Each canton and half-canton counts, so 25 until 1975 and 26 from 1979, when Jura became a canton. Cantons set their own terms and election dates: before the mid-1970s some elected their members every year or two, and in several the cantonal parliament elected them. Every such election, and every runoff, counts under the National Council election that follows it; an election held a year early, as Graubünden and Zug did until 2002 and 2006, counts with the next one. A show of hands at a Landsgemeinde, as in Appenzell Innerrhoden, leaves no vote count, and neither does an unopposed (tacit) election. So the archive counts both as complete once it records who was elected.

classes.name: Wahl des Bundesrates durch die Vereinigte Bundesversammlung
classes.name_en: Federal Council elections (by the Federal Assembly)
classes.note: The United Federal Assembly elects the seven members one seat at a time after each National Council renewal, in order of seniority of the incumbents, and fills vacancies in the session after a resignation (BV Art. 175; ParlG Art. 132 and 133). Each seat is one contest; ballots continue until a candidate passes the absolute majority of valid ballots.

cadence.runoff_rule: Absolute majority of valid ballots; anyone eligible may receive votes in the first two ballots, no new candidates from the third, and from then on the candidate with the fewest votes drops out (ParlG Art. 130 and 132).
cadence.vacancy_rule: Vacancies are filled as a rule in the session after the resignation or death (ParlG Art. 133).
cadence.locator: https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2003/510/de#art_132

classes.note: Elected each December for one year from among the members of the Federal Council; immediate re-election is barred (BV Art. 176).

classes.name: Wahlen der Kantonsparlamente (Kantonsrat, Grosser Rat, Landrat, Grand Conseil, Gran Consiglio, Parlement)
classes.note: Every canton elects a unicameral parliament, all by list proportional representation today except Appenzell Innerrhoden (majority vote in the districts) and, for some seats, Graubünden before 2022; constituencies are districts, communes, or regions set by each canton. Terms are four years except Fribourg, Vaud, Geneva, and Jura (five). Each canton's general election counts once. The listed years are those the Federal Statistical Office gives per canton in its four-year windows from 1968 to spring 2024, so cantons with three-year terms before the 2000s (Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Graubünden) are short a year in some windows. Elections after spring 2024 are listed by date from each canton's own announcement or results.

classes.note: Every canton's constitution and its amendments need the people's approval (BV Art. 51), and every canton has the initiative and a mandatory or optional referendum on laws, many also on spending. classes.name: Landsgemeinde
classes.note: The citizens of Glarus (first Sunday in May) and Appenzell Innerrhoden (last Sunday in April) meet in the open air to pass laws and the budget, and in Innerrhoden to elect the government, judges, and the Council of States member, all by show of hands, so there are outcomes but no vote counts. Abolished in Obwalden (1998), Nidwalden (1996), Appenzell Ausserrhoden (1997), Uri (1928), and Schwyz and Zug (1848).

classes.name: Wahlen der kantonalen Verfassungsräte
classes.note: A canton that totally revises its constitution may have the people elect a constitutional council (Verfassungsrat, Constituante) to draft it, as several did from the late 1990s (among them Vaud, Basel-Stadt, Zurich, Geneva, and Valais). Irregular; no federal list exists.

classes.name: Wahlen der Bezirksbehörden (Statthalter, Bezirksrat, Regierungsstatthalter, Bezirksammann)
classes.note: In several cantons the voters of each district elect its officials: in Zurich the Statthalter and the Bezirksrat (KV ZH Art. 80), in Bern a Regierungsstatthalter for each administrative region (KV BE), in Schwyz the district councils and parliaments (KV SZ § 27), and in Appenzell Innerrhoden the district councils at the Bezirksgemeinden. Elsewhere district officials are appointed or there are no districts.

classes.name: Bezirksabstimmungen und Bezirksgemeinden
classes.note: The districts of Schwyz and Appenzell Innerrhoden are self-governing corporations whose voters decide district business at the ballot box or in a Bezirksgemeinde (KV SZ; KV AI Art. 33 to 38).

classes.name: Volkswahl von Richterinnen und Richtern (Bezirks- und Amtsgerichte, Gerichtspräsidien, Friedensrichter)
classes.name_en: Popular election of judges and justices of the peace
classes.note: Several cantons have the people elect lower-court judges: Zurich the district courts (KV ZH Art. 75 and 80), Schwyz the district courts (KV SZ § 27), Basel-Stadt its court presidents (KV BS), and others their justices of the peace (Friedensrichter, juges de paix) by commune or circle. Higher cantonal judges are elected by the cantonal parliaments in all cantons.

classes.name: Wahlen der Gemeindeparlamente (Gemeinderat, Grosser Gemeinderat, Einwohnerrat, Stadtrat, Conseil communal, Conseil général, Consiglio comunale)
classes.note: Only some communes have an elected parliament (all communes in Geneva and Neuchâtel, communes above a size threshold in Vaud and Ticino, the cities elsewhere); the rest decide in a communal assembly. No federal register lists which communes have one. Terms follow the canton (KV ZH Art. 87: a commune may replace its assembly with a parliament). The archive counts the communes with a parliament in each canton from the cantonal lists, and expects their elections where the canton fixes one cycle for all of them: Lucerne, Fribourg, Solothurn, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Jura, Vaud, Neuchâtel, and Geneva, and Riehen in Basel-Stadt. Jura has five (Haute-Sorne, Val Terbi, Les Bois, Delémont, and Porrentruy; Moutier from 2026). Ticino has no official list yet. classes.name: Wahlen der Gemeindeexekutiven (Gemeinderat, Stadtrat, Municipalité, Conseil communal, Municipio)
classes.note: The voters of each commune elect its executive, at the ballot box or in the communal assembly, mostly by majority vote with a second round; Ticino's municipi and the executives in some other cantons by proportional representation (KV TI Art. 18). Two cantons differ: in Neuchâtel each commune decides whether its voters or its Conseil général elect the executive, and in Basel-Stadt the canton runs the city of Basel, so only Riehen and Bettingen elect one. The term is four years in most cantons and five in Fribourg, Vaud, Geneva, and Jura. Schwyz renews half of each council every two years, and the districts of Appenzell Innerrhoden elect theirs every year. Bern, Uri, Graubünden, and Basel-Stadt leave the term to each commune. The archive expects a yearly count only where cantonal law fixes the cycle for every commune, and one election each for Riehen, Bettingen, and the four Neuchâtel communes whose voters elected their executive in 2024 (Cressier, La Chaux-de-Fonds, Le Locle, and Neuchâtel). Foreigners vote in communal elections in Neuchâtel, Jura, Vaud, Fribourg, and Geneva, and in some communes of Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Graubünden, and Basel-Stadt.

classes.name: Gemeindeabstimmungen an der Urne
classes.note: Communes with a parliament, and many without, put budgets, credits, and bylaws to a ballot-box vote, mostly on federal vote days. Cantonal statistical offices publish some (Zurich's open data); there is no national collection.

classes.name: Gemeindeversammlung, assemblée communale, assemblea comunale
classes.note: Most Swiss communes decide their budget, accounts, and bylaws, and in many cantons elect their executive, in an assembly of all voters.
classes.disposition_reason: Assemblies decide by show of hands; the outcome stands only in each commune's minutes, with no count and no cantonal or national record to load from.

classes.name: Wahlen der Schulbehörden (Schulpflege, Schulkommission, Schulrat, Schulgemeinden)
classes.note: In Zurich, Thurgau, Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, and other German-speaking cantons the voters of the commune or of a separate school commune (Schulgemeinde) elect the school board; Zurich city elects one per school circle (Kreisschulbehörde). In the French- and Italian-speaking cantons schools are run by the commune executive.

cadence.locator: GPR ZH § 40 lit. a Ziff. 3 (the Schulpflege is elected at the ballot box); § 32 Abs. 1 (four years)
GG SH Art. 6 Abs. 2 lit. d (the president and members of the Schulbehörde are elected at the ballot box); KV SH Art. 41 Abs. 1 (four years)

classes.name: Wahlen der Bürger- und Burgergemeinden (Bürgerrat, Burgerrat, conseil bourgeoisial, patriziato)
classes.note: Public-law corporations of the citizens (Bürger) of a commune by descent, which hold property and in some cantons grant citizenship; their councils are elected by members only, in Valais with the communal councils (KV VS: 'die Gemeinderäte und die Burgerräte sind für eine Amtsdauer von vier Jahren gewählt').

cadence.locator: KV OW Art. 98 Abs. 1 Ziff. 1: the Bürgergemeindeversammlung elects a Bürgergemeinderat of five to nine members for four years
GemG BL § 142 Abs. 1 and 2 (the president, the Bürgerrat, and the Bürgerkommission are elected at the ballot box by majority vote); § 12 Abs. 1 (four years)
Cst. VS art. 85: the Burgerräte are elected for four years, like the communal councils

classes.name: Wahlen und Abstimmungen der Kirchgemeinden der Landeskirchen
classes.name_en: Parish elections of the recognized churches
classes.disposition_reason: Church members only, run by the recognized churches and their parishes (pastors, parish councils, synods), not by the communes' electoral authorities for all residents.

classes.name: Korporationen, Genossenschaften, Zünfte, Alpgenossenschaften
classes.disposition_reason: Property-holding corporations and guilds (Oberallmeind- and Unterallmeindkorporationen, Alpgenossenschaften, Zünfte) whose members are owners or descendants, not a territorial electorate.

classes.name: Kammer-, Hochschul-, Personal- und Parteiwahlen
classes.name_en: Professional, university, staff, and party-internal votes
classes.disposition_reason: Votes run by professional bodies, universities, employers, the Organisation of the Swiss Abroad, and parties for their own members; Swiss parties hold no state-run primaries.

classes.name: Volksabstimmung über die Verfassung der Helvetischen Republik 1802
classes.note: The first popular vote held in Switzerland: the second Helvetic constitution, declared accepted on 2 July 1802, with abstentions counted as yes votes.

dates.quote: Nach der ersten in der Schweiz durchgeführten Volksabstimmung, bei der die Nichtstimmenden als Befürworter gezählt wurden ( Abstimmungen ), galt sie am 2. Juli als angenommen.

classes.name: Urversammlungen und Wahlmännerversammlungen der Helvetischen Republik
classes.name_en: Primary and electoral assemblies of the Helvetic Republic
classes.note: Citizens met each year in primary assemblies in their communes to choose electors, and each canton's electoral assembly then chose the members of the Senate and Great Council and the cantonal authorities.
